name: macOS app switches
summary: Notices when you switch to a designated Mac app, by bundle id and nothing else.
description: A single-file Swift program that listens for macOS's app-activation notification, maps the app's bundle id onto your designated apps, and drops everything else on your Mac before anything is sent. It reads no window titles, URLs or content, so it needs no Accessibility or Screen Recording permission. It is an untested spike: this build environment has no macOS, so it has never been compiled or run.

emits.when: You switch to VS Code, Zed, Xcode or IntelliJ
You switch to Terminal, iTerm2, Warp or Ghostty
You switch to Notes, Obsidian or Notion
You switch to the Claude desktop app

neverSends: Window titles, or anything a window shows
Apps you haven't designated: they're dropped on your Mac, before anything is sent

setup.title: Run the sensor
setup.body: It runs until you press Ctrl-C, and re-reads your designated apps from FocusDeck every minute.

setup.title: Optional: compile it once
setup.body: A compiled binary starts instantly; run it from a login item if you want it always on.

test.expect: {"accepted":1,…} and "Switched to Editor" in Today's log. This checks the bridge and your designation, not the Swift program itself.
